newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil close to securitizing housing fund debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil close to securitizing housing fund debt.

text.p: The Brazilian government is close to securitizing a billion real shortfall in a federal housing fund, with only a few legal problems to work out, Finance Minister Pedro Malan reportedly said on Wednesday.

The private Invest News agency said Malan told reporters the government intended to use 30-year Treasury notes, with a 15-year grace period for principle and eight years grace for interest, to securitize the black hole.
He added that it remained unclear how large the shortfall in the so-called FCVS housing fund really was. Independent analysts have put it at about $50 billion.
Populist housing policies since the FCVS fund was created in 1967 have allowed mortgage holders to repay only a portion of their debt.

Malan said the government had concluded the technical details of a decree allowing the Treasury to start securitizing the debt. He said only a few legal issues remained to be solved, acording to Invest News.

Malan said 15 percent of FCVS contracts were no longer accepted because the government discovered the beneficiaries had other contracts. But he said the government had already recognized 12 billion reais as debt.
The minister said the decree would create incentives for debtors to pay off their FCVS credit contracts early.
Reports in July suggested the National Treasury expected to begin issuing between 15 billion reais and 20 billion reais in notes at the end of the year to start covering the deficit.
Government officials have stressed the operation would not place too great a burden on public accounts, as it involved exchanging old debt for new.
